newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Local buys support Russian shares.
newsitem.headline: Local buys support Russian shares.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed on domestic buying on Tuesday, traders said, but they differed on the reasons for the buying activity and some forecast the market would resume its downward trend in the short term.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed slightly up at 423.87 from Monday's 418.63 close.
"Local brokers have started to take positions," said Regent European Securities broker Alexander Fonarkov, adding domestic players were encouraged by the absence of selling on the market.
"It is an attempt to play the market up, since there is an expectation the market won't collapse in the next few days."
Oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS rose to $20.20 from $19.63, while national electricity company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.3724 from $0.3619.

International long-distance provider Rostelekom RTKM.RTS rose as high as $4.00 after it posted a rise in 1996 net profits prepared to international standards to 1.71 trillion roubles from 1.40 trillion in 1995.
It also said it was ready to issue level-two ADRs after approval by a new board of directors later this month. Shares closed at $3.97 after $3.88 on Monday.

United Financial Group trader Igor Vain said short covering was partly the cause of the market firming, along with both Western and Russian investors taking positions, particularly in LUKoil, at the start of the second half of the year.
"Today the market got a push in the blue chips, first and foremost from LUKoil," said Vain. "Even at its historical maximum shares in the company are are undervalued."
But Bank MFK (ICFI) deputy head of stock market operations Alexei Abdurakhimov said the rise was just a blip in the general downward trend.
"The market will now fall and fluctuate a little," Abdurakhimov said. "This is not even a correction, just a little nervous jump."
